**Status:** DRAFT — first planning pass. Synthesised from a hand-off package (a research
prototype built in an earlier session, archived verbatim as `source-*.md`) and reconciled with
this repo's conventions. No code written yet.
**Companion doc:** [`design.md`](./design.md) — repo layout, components, the feature contract,
the `RiskAssessment` shape, scoring-mode semantics, the FHIR mapping sketch, artifacts, the
agent's tool contract, testing, and the prototype defects found in review.
**Milestone plan:** [`milestone-plan.md`](./milestone-plan.md) — M1–M11, kept as its own
document, same convention as Phase 6 (`phase6/decisions.md` H23) and Phase 7.
**Decision index:** [`decisions.md`](./decisions.md) — `O1`–`O27`.
**Source (input, not contract):** [`source-prd.md`](./source-prd.md),
[`source-design.md`](./source-design.md), [`source-developer-notes.md`](./source-developer-notes.md).
§11 below lists every deviation from them.
**Extends:** Phase 1 (`fhir-service`, `client/clinical` — extended additively), Phase 6
(`agent-platform` — the new agent is built on it). Reads the Synthea data pipeline already in
`data/`.
**Owner:** repo owner.

---

## 1. Problem statement

Primary-care teams in value-based contracts — especially risk-bearing practices serving
Medicare patients — are paid to keep patients out of hospital. They need a ranked list of who
is most likely to be admitted in the next year, with reasons, so care managers can reach out
early. Commercial risk scores exist but are proprietary, expensive, and trained on data nobody
can inspect.

Phase 8 adds the platform's first **machine-learned** clinical capability: an inspectable,
reproducible model, trained only on free, open, US data, that estimates each adult's
probability of at least one inpatient stay in the next 12 months — and returns it the way the
rest of this platform returns clinical judgements, as a FHIR `RiskAssessment` (O3).

It is a different kind of clinical logic from everything before it. `triage-service`'s rules
are deterministic and hand-auditable; a gradient-boosting model is deterministic at inference
but not hand-auditable. Two consequences shape this PRD: every score ships **beside a simple,
hand-checkable comparison score** and its top reasons, and every reported metric must be
**reproducible from public data with one command per stage**.

## 2. Decisions already made (see `decisions.md`)

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| What is predicted | Any inpatient stay in the 12 months after the as-of date, adults 18+ (O1). |
| Where the model runs | One new service, `outcome-prediction-service/` (O2). |
| What it returns | FHIR `RiskAssessment` with `probabilityDecimal`; Phase 8's own models, `triage-service` untouched (O3). |
| Phase numbering | Hand-off "Phase 0–4" → milestones M1–M11 + Phase 8b (O4). |
| Hand-off documents | Archived verbatim, non-normative (O5). |
| Order of work | Reproduce the prototype's numbers before changing any logic (O6). |
| Training data | MEPS longitudinal panels 21–27 (2016–2023), carried over from the hand-off; commercial use still unconfirmed (O23). |
| Input path | FHIR from `fhir-service` via `client/clinical`, this phase (O8, O9). |
| Agent | New `outcome-prediction-agent/` on `agent-platform`; `mcp-agent` untouched; self-hosted LLM by default (O15, O16). |
| Exposure | Internal-only; no Kong route (O14). |

## 3. Goals

- **G1 — Reproduce the prototype.** Rebuild the MEPS modelling table (56,360 adults, 4,820
  events), the gradient-boosting model (temporal-test AUROC 0.769) and the comparison model
  (0.708) inside this repo, within the source tolerances, with tests.
- **G2 — A reproducible training pipeline.** Download, build, train, evaluate: one command per
  stage, fixed seeds, pinned versions, recorded data checksums, machine-readable and readable
  reports.
- **G3 — One versioned feature contract.** Every source — MEPS for training, Synthea CSV for
  reproduction, FHIR in production — is converted to the same versioned schema (`meps25-v1`
  first). The model only ever sees that schema.
- **G4 — Score a real FHIR patient.** Given a patient in `fhir-service` and an as-of date, derive
  the contract features from their FHIR record and return a `RiskAssessment`.
- **G5 — Leakage-proof scoring.** Scoring mode never reads a record dated after `as_of`, and a
  test proves it (O10).
- **G6 — Explainable output.** Every result carries the main probability, the comparison-model
  probability, a population percentile, the model and contract versions, top contributing
  features, and references to the FHIR resources it was derived from.
- **G7 — Grounded conversational access.** A clinician can ask, in natural language, for a
  patient's hospitalization risk and its reasons; the agent relays the service's output and
  introduces no fact of its own.
- **G8 — A better label and model (second half of the phase).** An unplanned-stay label that
  excludes childbirth/pregnancy stays, richer condition and drug features, panel-grouped
  tuning, and specific attention to adults 65+.

## 4. Non-goals

- **The agent never computes, adjusts, or infers a risk score.** Same boundary as every agent
  in this repo (CLAUDE.md: "the agent orchestrates but holds no clinical logic").
- **No real patient data reaches any LLM or online service.** Development uses MEPS public
  files and Synthea only (O16).
- **No free-text features.** The training data has none.
- **Not a real-time or emergency tool.** A yearly planning score.
- **No diagnosis or treatment recommendation.**
- **No customer data in this repository,** for training or fixtures.
- **No UK or other non-US data sources.** (Rejected with reasons in `source-prd.md` §5.)
- **No CPT codes** (AMA licence).
- **Synthea results are never evidence of accuracy.** Every report that includes them says so.
- **No qualitative band (high/moderate/low)** until thresholds are clinically signed off (O24).
- **No changes to `triage-service`, `mcp-agent`, or the Kong gateway.**

| User | Need | Served by |
|---|---|---|
| Care manager / nurse | Ranked patients, with reasons | Scoring API + percentile + top reasons (worklist UI deferred, §8) |
| Primary-care clinician | One patient's risk, easy to sanity-check | Agent (G7) or API; comparison score beside the main score |
| Population-health lead | Calibrated risk; subgroup performance | Evaluation reports (FR-E*) |
| Customer IT / data engineering | A documented input schema | Feature contract + FHIR adapter |
| Repo owner | Reproducible pipeline, licence position, a sellable platform | G1–G2, O13, O23 |

# Phase 8 Design — Patient Outcome Prediction

Architecture, component breakdown, and the technical sketches `milestone-plan.md` builds
against. Status and requirements live in [`README.md`](./README.md) and [`prd.md`](./prd.md).
The hand-off's preliminary design is archived as [`source-design.md`](./source-design.md);
where this document is silent, that one is still the best description of intent — but where
they disagree, this one wins.

## 1. Repo layout

```
outcome-prediction-service/       # NEW (O2) — training pipeline, ETL, scoring API; no conversational logic
  pyproject.toml                  # requires-python >=3.11; scikit-learn pinned exactly (O12)
  README.md                       # service-level detail, per docs/README.md conventions
  src/outcome_prediction/
    meps/
      download.py                 # FR-D1: fetch h{n}dta.zip, extract with zipfile, record SHA-256
      build.py                    # FR-D2: modelling table + label(s)
      inspect.py                  # FR-D3: variable dictionary
    model/
      train.py                    # FR-M1–M4: validation model (21–25) + release model (all panels)
      evaluate.py                 # FR-E1–E6: metrics.json + model_report.md
      artifact.py                 # write/verify artifact dir + SHA-256 manifest (O17)
    contract.py                   # feature contracts (meps25-v1, later v2), Pydantic, feature order
    etl/
      canonical.py                # the five canonical tables (§7)
      extract/synthea_csv.py      # reproduction/parity harness (O8)
      extract/fhir.py             # NEW vs. hand-off: canonical tables from client/clinical (M5)
      transform/to_contract.py    # canonical → contract rows; training vs scoring mode (§6)
      codelists/                  # M11: versioned ICD-10-CM 3-char lists per flag
    fhir/
      risk_assessment.py          # Phase 8's own RiskAssessment/Bundle models + builder (O3, §4)
    api.py                        # FastAPI app (§5)
    tools.py                      # the tool surface outcome-prediction-agent may call (§9)
  tests/
    fixtures/                     # tiny committed Synthea sample + synthetic contract rows (no MEPS)
  models/                         # gitignored — built artifacts
  data/                           # gitignored — MEPS cache, Synthea CSV/FHIR outputs

outcome-prediction-agent/         # NEW (O15) — conversational layer, own top-level package
  src/outcome_prediction_agent/
    agent.py                      # tool-use loop on agent-platform (Phase 6)
    explain.py                    # grounded narration of a RiskAssessment (FR-A2, FR-A3)

client/clinical/                  # extended additively (O9, FR-F1)
e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py   # M8
```

Not created: a separate `hosp-risk/` repo, a Makefile, a second devcontainer, a second CI
workflow, `LICENSES.md` (`prd.md` §11 V2, V7). `mcp-agent/`, `triage-service/` and
`gateway/` are untouched.

**Dependency direction.** `outcome-prediction-agent` → `outcome-prediction-service` (HTTP, via
`tools.py`'s contract) and → `agent-platform`. It does **not** import `client/clinical`,
`triage-service`, or any model code. `outcome-prediction-service` → `client/clinical` → the
FHIR server. Nothing in earlier phases depends on anything in Phase 8.

## 2. Component responsibilities

| Component | Responsibility | Consumes | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meps/*` | Acquire, check, and shape MEPS public files | AHRQ URLs | Cached `.dta` + checksums; modelling table; dictionaries |
| `model/train.py` | Fit the GBM and comparison model | Modelling table | Artifact directory (§8) |
| `model/evaluate.py` | Temporal-test metrics | Modelling table, validation model | `metrics.json`, `model_report.md` |
| `contract.py` | Single source of truth for feature names, types, allowed values, order | — | Pydantic models; validators |
| `etl/extract/*` | Source-specific reading only — no feature logic | Synthea CSV, or `client/clinical` | Canonical tables |
| `etl/transform/to_contract.py` | All feature logic, once, for every source | Canonical tables, `as_of`, mode | Contract rows (+ label in training mode) + per-feature provenance |
| `fhir/risk_assessment.py` | Build FHIR output | Scores, explanations, provenance | `RiskAssessment` / `Bundle` |
| `api.py` | HTTP surface, artifact loading, validation | Requests | §5 |

   at 0; `score.py` doesn't. Moot once the API rejects negatives, but `to_contract.py` applies
   one rule for both modes.
5. **Reported metrics belong to a different model object**: the release model is refit on all
   panels, so its own held-out performance is unknown. `metadata.json` says so explicitly and
   carries the validation model's metrics labelled as such.
6. **Diagnosis-column resolution by prefix** (`build_meps_hosp12.py`): "first column starting
   with the prefix and containing `Y1`" is fragile across panels. M1 logs the resolved column
   per panel per flag into the build report, so a silent mismatch is visible.

# Phase 8 Design — Patient Outcome Prediction

Architecture, component breakdown, and the technical sketches `milestone-plan.md` builds
against. Status and requirements live in [`README.md`](./README.md) and [`prd.md`](./prd.md).
The hand-off's preliminary design is archived as [`source-design.md`](./source-design.md);
where this document is silent, that one is still the best description of intent — but where
they disagree, this one wins.

## 1. Repo layout

```
outcome-prediction-service/       # NEW (O2) — training pipeline, ETL, scoring API; no conversational logic
  pyproject.toml                  # requires-python >=3.11; scikit-learn pinned exactly (O12)
  README.md                       # service-level detail, per docs/README.md conventions
  src/outcome_prediction/
    meps/
      download.py                 # FR-D1: fetch h{n}dta.zip, extract with zipfile, record SHA-256
      build.py                    # FR-D2: modelling table + label(s)
      inspect.py                  # FR-D3: variable dictionary
    model/
      train.py                    # FR-M1–M4: validation model (21–25) + release model (all panels)
      evaluate.py                 # FR-E1–E6: metrics.json + model_report.md
      artifact.py                 # write/verify artifact dir + SHA-256 manifest (O17)
    contract.py                   # feature contracts (meps25-v1, later v2), Pydantic, feature order
    etl/
      canonical.py                # the five canonical tables (§7)
      extract/synthea_csv.py      # reproduction/parity harness (O8)
      extract/fhir.py             # NEW vs. hand-off: canonical tables from client/clinical (M5)
      transform/to_contract.py    # canonical → contract rows; training vs scoring mode (§6)
      codelists/                  # M11: versioned ICD-10-CM 3-char lists per flag
    fhir/
      risk_assessment.py          # Phase 8's own RiskAssessment/Bundle models + builder (O3, §4)
    api.py                        # FastAPI app (§5)
    tools.py                      # the tool surface outcome-prediction-agent may call (§9)
  tests/
    fixtures/                     # tiny committed Synthea sample + synthetic contract rows (no MEPS)
  models/                         # gitignored — built artifacts
  data/                           # gitignored — MEPS cache, Synthea CSV/FHIR outputs

outcome-prediction-agent/         # NEW (O15) — conversational layer, own top-level package
  src/outcome_prediction_agent/
    agent.py                      # tool-use loop on agent-platform (Phase 6)
    explain.py                    # grounded narration of a RiskAssessment (FR-A2, FR-A3)

client/clinical/                  # extended additively (O9, FR-F1)
e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py   # M8
```

Not created: a separate `hosp-risk/` repo, a Makefile, a second devcontainer, a second CI
workflow, `LICENSES.md` (`prd.md` §11 V2, V7). `mcp-agent/`, `triage-service/` and
`gateway/` are untouched.

**Dependency direction.** `outcome-prediction-agent` → `outcome-prediction-service` (HTTP, via
`tools.py`'s contract) and → `agent-platform`. It does **not** import `client/clinical`,
`triage-service`, or any model code. `outcome-prediction-service` → `client/clinical` → the
FHIR server. Nothing in earlier phases depends on anything in Phase 8.

## 2. Component responsibilities

| Component | Responsibility | Consumes | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meps/*` | Acquire, check, and shape MEPS public files | AHRQ URLs | Cached `.dta` + checksums; modelling table; dictionaries |
| `model/train.py` | Fit the GBM and comparison model | Modelling table | Artifact directory (§8) |
| `model/evaluate.py` | Temporal-test metrics | Modelling table, validation model | `metrics.json`, `model_report.md` |
| `contract.py` | Single source of truth for feature names, types, allowed values, order | — | Pydantic models; validators |
| `etl/extract/*` | Source-specific reading only — no feature logic | Synthea CSV, or `client/clinical` | Canonical tables |
| `etl/transform/to_contract.py` | All feature logic, once, for every source | Canonical tables, `as_of`, mode | Contract rows (+ label in training mode) + per-feature provenance |
| `fhir/risk_assessment.py` | Build FHIR output | Scores, explanations, provenance | `RiskAssessment` / `Bundle` |
| `api.py` | HTTP surface, artifact loading, validation | Requests | §5 |
| `tools.py` | The *only* functions the agent can reach | — | §9 |

The hand-off's principle 1 ("one feature contract") is enforced structurally: extractors may
not compute features; only `to_contract.py` does, so a mapping fix lands once for every source.

## 3. The feature contract `meps25-v1`

Carried over unchanged from `source-design.md` §4: 25 required integer features, MEPS codes,
negatives rejected at the API, and this exact column order:

```
sex, racethx, regiony1, agey1x, inscovy1, povcaty1, ipdisy1, ipngtdy1, ertoty1, obtotvy1,
optotvy1, hhtotdy1, rxtoty1, totexpy1, hibpdx, chddx, angidx, midx, ohrtdx, strkdx, emphdx,
diabdx, arthdx, asthdx, choldx
```

Two interpretation changes, both from review (§11):

- In scoring mode, every `*y1` feature means **the 12 months ending at `as_of`** (O10). The
  names keep MEPS' `y1` suffix because the model was trained on them; the window is documented
  in `contract.py`, not encoded in the name.
- `regiony1 = 0` for an unknown or non-US state, as the contract always said; the prototype's
  default to South (3) is not carried over.

`meps25-v2` (M9) pairs the contract with `label_unplanned_12m`; feature changes from O25/FR-D5
arrive as a new contract version, never as an edit to an existing one. The service serves one
contract version per loaded artifact and rejects requests that name another.

## 4. The `RiskAssessment` (O3)

Phase 8 defines its own Pydantic models — a superset of `triage-service`'s, which has no
numeric probability. Shape:

```
RiskAssessment
  status: final
  subject: Patient/{id}                       # or identifier, for contract-row scoring
  occurrenceDateTime: as_of
  method: CodeableConcept                     # model id, e.g. gbm-meps25-<date>; system http://fhir-agent.local/outcome-prediction/model
  basis: [Encounter/…, Condition/…, MedicationRequest/…, ExplanationOfBenefit/…]   # FR-F4; empty for contract rows
  prediction[0]:
    outcome: SNOMED CT 32485007 "Hospital admission (procedure)"                 # O22, verify in M6
    probabilityDecimal: 0.31
    whenPeriod: { start: as_of, end: as_of + 12 months }
    rationale: "Top factors: age, prior inpatient stay, prescription fills."      # templated from top_reasons
    extension:
      - url: …/comparison-probability   valueDecimal: 0.29                       # FR-S2 / O18
      - url: …/risk-percentile          valueInteger: 94
      - url: …/contract-version         valueString: meps25-v1
      - url: …/top-reasons              valueString: agey1x                        # repeated, ordered
  note[0]: "12-month planning estimate, not a diagnosis. Trained on MEPS public data; …"
  extension:
      - url: …/input-warning            valueString: …                            # out-of-range inputs, defaults applied
```

- **No `qualitativeRisk`** until thresholds are signed off (O24). This is the deliberate
  difference from `triage-service`'s output.
- **Extensions vs. a second `prediction`.** A second `prediction` element would claim a second
  *outcome*; the comparison model predicts the same outcome with a different method, so it is
  an extension on the one prediction. Extension URLs live under
  `http://fhir-agent.local/StructureDefinition/` (the namespace `triage-service` already uses
  for its codes); formal `StructureDefinition`s are not written this phase.
- `rationale` text is **templated** from `top_reasons`, never model-generated — same principle
  as Phase 7 R20.
- Batches return a FHIR `Bundle` of type `collection`.

## 5. API

Matches `triage-service`'s route style (no `/v1` prefix; `/health` at root):

| Method and path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | Liveness; reports whether an artifact is loaded and verified |
| `GET /model` | Model ID, contract version, training summary, headline metrics, library versions |
| `POST /risk/hospitalization-12m` | Trigger A: `{patient_id, as_of?}` → fetch via `client/clinical`, transform, score → `RiskAssessment` |
| `POST /risk/hospitalization-12m/contract-rows` | Trigger B: `{contract_version, rows: [{patient_ref, features}]}` (1–1,000) → `Bundle` |

Internal-only, no Kong route (O14). Port: the next free one in the `800x` range, assigned in M6.
Compose: a `phase8` profile service that depends on `fhir`, plus a read-only volume for the
artifact directory.

## 6. Training mode vs scoring mode (O10)

| | Training mode | Scoring mode |
|---|---|---|
| Who uses it | MEPS build; Synthea CSV reproduction | The API; the FHIR extractor |
| Feature window | Calendar year Y (reproduction) | 12 months ending `as_of` |
| Label | Year Y+1 | None — never computed |
| May read records after the window | Yes, to build the label only | **No — filtered at the extractor boundary** |

The filter is applied once, in the extractor, before any transform runs: canonical tables in
scoring mode contain nothing dated after `as_of`. Records that *span* `as_of` (a medication
active across it, an inpatient stay admitted before and discharged after) are truncated at
`as_of` — never extrapolated from their eventual end.

**Mandatory test** (`source-design.md` §7 "Leakage", now load-bearing): for a fixture patient,
add and remove records dated after `as_of` — including a long-running prescription whose stop
date and dispense count are only known later — and assert identical contract rows.

## 7. Canonical model and the FHIR mapping sketch (O21 — unvalidated)

Canonical tables carried over from `source-design.md` §3.6.1 (`person`, `coverage`,
`encounter`, `condition`, `medication_fill`), with one added column on each: `source_ref` (the
FHIR `Type/id`, or the CSV row ID) — what makes FR-F4's `basis` possible.

The FHIR extractor's sketch — **every row to be confirmed against real Synthea v4.0.0 output in
M5**, recording what was found, as Phase 7 does for RxNav (R11):

| Canonical | FHIR source (via `client/clinical`) | Known risk |
|---|---|---|
| `person` | `Patient` (gender, birthDate, deceased, address.state; race/ethnicity from US Core extensions) | Income and household size absent → `povcaty1` defaulted with a warning; ZIP-level income is a later contract version (`source-design.md` §9.2) |
| `encounter` | `Encounter.class` + `period` | Synthea maps several CSV classes to `AMB`; office vs hospital-outpatient (`obtotvy1` vs `optotvy1`) may need `Encounter.type`/`serviceType`, or a documented merge |
| `condition` | `Condition` code (SNOMED) + onset | Description regex (prototype) until M11's code lists |
| `medication_fill` | `MedicationDispense` if present; else `MedicationRequest` + `dispenseRequest`, truncated at `as_of` | Synthea's FHIR may not carry a dispense count; the fallback rule is decided and documented in M5 |
| `coverage` | `Coverage`, or `ExplanationOfBenefit.insurance` | Which one Synthea v4.0.0 populates is unverified |
| cost (`totexpy1`) | `ExplanationOfBenefit` payment/total, else `Claim.total` | Charges vs MEPS payments (O25) |

Synthea runs for Phase 8 (O11) override `exporter.csv.export=true` and
`exporter.years_of_history` on the command line so both formats and enough history come from
one run; the shared `data/synthea/synthea.properties` is not edited.

## 8. Model artifacts (O17, O18)

```
models/<model_id>/
  model.joblib          # GBM
  comparison.joblib     # logistic regression (O18)
  metadata.json         # features + order, categoricals, contract version, training panels,
                        # row/event counts, data checksums, library versions, git commit, metrics,
                        # training-population score distribution (for percentiles)
  MANIFEST.sha256       # verified before any deserialisation; mismatch → refuse to start
```

Never committed. CI trains a throwaway model on a committed synthetic contract-row fixture so
service tests run without MEPS; MEPS-dependent tests (M1–M2 reproduction) self-skip when the
cache is absent, like `provider-registry-service`'s DB tests. Percentiles are computed against
the training population this phase; per-customer percentiles arrive with recalibration
(Phase 8b).

## 9. The agent's tool contract (O15)

`tools.py` (in `outcome-prediction-service`) defines exactly what `outcome-prediction-agent`
can call:

| Tool | What it does | What it cannot do |
|---|---|---|
| `find_patient(name)` | Candidate search via `client/clinical`; returns ID, name, birth date | Cannot auto-pick among several candidates — ambiguity goes back to the human |
| `get_hospitalization_risk(patient_id, as_of?)` | Calls the scoring path; returns the `RiskAssessment` | Read-only; no parameters touch features or the model |
| `get_model_card()` | Returns `/model` metadata for "how was this built?" questions | Read-only |

**There is no tool that accepts feature values, a threshold, or a model choice.** The agent
can't "re-score with a different age" or "flag anyone over 20%", because those would put
clinical logic in the agent. `explain.py`'s system prompt allows only facts present in the
returned `RiskAssessment` (FR-A2), plus the fixed planning-aid statement (FR-A3); the
agent-turn output gate follows `agent-platform`'s `output_gate.py` pattern.

## 10. Testing strategy

Carried over from `source-design.md` §7, mapped to this repo:

| Level | What | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Every mapping rule, incl. the regression: "Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat" must not set `chddx` | `phase8` CI job |
| Contract | Pydantic rejects missing fields, wrong types, out-of-range codes, wrong contract version | CI |
| Leakage | §6 test, both extractors | CI |
| Parity | FR-F3, on a small committed Synthea CSV + FHIR fixture from one run | CI |
| Artifact | Tampered manifest → service refuses to start | CI |
| Data | Per-panel row counts equal `source-prd.md` §9 | Local; self-skips without MEPS cache |
| Model | Test AUROC within tolerance; metadata has the 25 features in order | Local; self-skips |
| Agent | Grounding + adversarial ("adjust the score", "call it high risk") | CI with the self-hosted model, same as Phase 6's adversarial suite |
| End to end | `e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py` against the `phase8` stack | Local, like the other e2e suites |

The root `pytest.ini` gains the new test paths; the Phase 1 independence job is unchanged.

## 11. Prototype defects found in review

Recorded here so M3–M6 fix them **after** the reproduction (O6), each with a test:

1. **Prescription-fill leakage** (`ehr_to_meps.py`): a missing medication `STOP` is filled with
   the end of year 2, and `DISPENSES` (a lifetime total known only later) is prorated across
   that span — so year-1 `rxtoty1` and `totexpy1` depend on future data. Fixed by §6.
2. **Comparison model not saved** (`train_model.py`): only the GBM is pickled, yet FR-S2 needs
   both scores. Fixed by O18.
3. **Unknown state → South** (`ehr_to_meps.py`): contradicts the contract's `0 if unknown`.
   Fixed in `to_contract.py`; no effect on the Arizona reproduction run.
4. **Categorical handling differs between training and scoring**: training clips categoricals
   at 0; `score.py` doesn't. Moot once the API rejects negatives, but `to_contract.py` applies
   one rule for both modes.
5. **Reported metrics belong to a different model object**: the release model is refit on all
   panels, so its own held-out performance is unknown. `metadata.json` says so explicitly and
   carries the validation model's metrics labelled as such.
6. **Diagnosis-column resolution by prefix** (`build_meps_hosp12.py`): "first column starting
   with the prefix and containing `Y1`" is fragile across panels. M1 logs the resolved column
   per panel per flag into the build report, so a silent mismatch is visible.

# Phase 8 Milestone Plan — Patient Outcome Prediction

M1–M11. All **planned, none started**.

Sequencing logic: **reproduce first** (M1–M3) — dataset, model, Synthea harness — so every later
number has a recorded baseline (O6). Then **make it usable end to end on the reproduced model**
(M4–M8): `client/clinical` plumbing, the FHIR extractor, the scoring service, the agent, and a
live acceptance case. Only then **improve the model** (M9–M11): better label, richer features,
code lists — each landing as a new contract version behind a service that already works.

This reverses the hand-off's order, which improved the model before building the service
(`prd.md` §11 V12). The reason is risk: the FHIR mapping (O21) and the leakage rule (O10) are
the least certain parts of the design, and they're exercised by the service path, not by MEPS.
Finding out early whether real Synthea FHIR can feed the contract matters more than a
0.01 AUROC gain.

Parallelism: after M3, **M4 → M5** (plumbing → extractor) and **M9** (label work, MEPS-only)
don't depend on each other and can run side by side. M6 needs M5; M7 needs M6.

## Mapping from the hand-off's phases (O4)

| Hand-off phase | Content | Here |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Research prototype | Provenance — `source-*.md` |
| 1 | Reproduce prototype with tests and reports | M1, M2, M3 |
| 2 | Better label, richer features, tuning, 65+, explanations | M9, M10 (explanations moved up to M6) |
| 3 | Scoring API, batch job, FHIR and claims adapters, code lists | M4, M5, M6, M11 (batch from object storage and claims adapter deferred — `prd.md` §8) |
| — | Agent surface, live acceptance case (this repo's conventions) | M7, M8 |
| 4 | Deployment, monitoring, recalibration, first customer validation | Phase 8b |

---

### M1 — Service scaffold + MEPS dataset

**Short story:** Stand up `outcome-prediction-service/` and rebuild the MEPS modelling table
exactly.

**Long story:** Package skeleton per `design.md` §1 (`pyproject.toml`, `README.md`,
gitignored `data/` and `models/`), `phase8` compose profile placeholder, `phase8` CI job,
`pytest.ini` entry. First, run the source's `build_meps_hosp12.py` and `inspect_meps.py` once
from a scratch location and record their output (O7). Then implement `meps/download.py`
(zipfile extraction, SHA-256 record), `meps/build.py` (with per-panel diagnosis-column
resolution logged — `design.md` §11 defect 6) and `meps/inspect.py`. Register MEPS in
`data/reference/README.md` with its use terms and the open AHRQ question (O13, O23).

**Deliverable:** 56,360 rows, 4,820 events, per-panel counts matching `source-prd.md` §9;
HC-252 dictionary with 2,648 variables and the expected storage counts. Phase 1 independence
job still green.

**Depends on:** nothing new.

---

### M2 — Training, evaluation, artifact

**Short story:** Reproduce AUROC 0.769 / 0.708 and write the reports.

**Long story:** `model/train.py`, `model/evaluate.py`, `model/artifact.py`. Reference numbers
from the source's `train_model.py`/`evaluate_model.py` recorded first (O7). The artifact
carries both models (O18), a SHA-256 manifest (O17), the training score distribution (for
percentiles), and metadata stating that headline metrics come from the validation model, not
the release model (`design.md` §11 defect 5). `scikit-learn` pinned exactly (O12).

**Deliverable:** Test AUROC in [0.760, 0.778] (GBM) and [0.700, 0.716] (comparison);
`metrics.json` + `model_report.md` covering FR-E1–E5; a tampered manifest is refused.

**Depends on:** M1.

---

### M3 — Synthea CSV harness, scoring mode, leakage test

**Short story:** Reproduce the Synthea ETL as-is, then split training from scoring mode and fix
the prescription leak.

**Long story:** Generate one Synthea v4.0.0 population with CSV **and** FHIR export (O11) —
the FHIR half is used in M5. Port `ehr_to_meps.py` into `etl/extract/synthea_csv.py` +
`etl/canonical.py` + `etl/transform/to_contract.py`; confirm schema and sanity checks
(`prd.md` §9.4). **Then**, as a separate commit: the `as_of` scoring mode (`design.md` §6),
the leakage test, unknown-state → 0, and one categorical rule for both modes (§11 defects 1, 3,
4). Commit a tiny Synthea fixture for CI; keep the `coronary` regression test.

**Deliverable:** Contract rows from Synthea CSV in both modes; the leakage test passes, and
fails on the reproduced (unfixed) code — proving it tests something.

**Depends on:** M2 (needs a model to score with).

---

### M4 — `client/clinical` extension (additive)

**Short story:** Give the clinical client the encounters, medication history and cost data the
contract needs, without changing anything existing callers see.

**Long story:** New domain dataclasses and methods (FR-F1), each returning clinical terms, never
raw bundles. Coordinate with Phase 7 M3 on `get_medications()`'s status filter — whichever
lands first defines it (O9). `triage-service`'s and `mcp-agent`'s test suites must pass
unmodified.

**Deliverable:** New methods with unit tests against recorded FHIR fixtures; all existing
`client/clinical` callers unaffected.

**Depends on:** nothing in Phase 8 beyond M1's scaffold; can start alongside M2–M3.

---

### M5 — FHIR extractor + parity + data-quality report

**Short story:** Build the canonical tables from `fhir-service`, and prove they match the CSV
path.

**Long story:** `etl/extract/fhir.py`. Load M3's FHIR half into `fhir-service`, then validate
every row of `design.md` §7's mapping sketch against what Synthea v4.0.0 actually emits —
recording each finding in the design doc (O21). The parity test (FR-F3) runs the same patients
through both extractors. Every feature records its contributing resources (FR-F4). The
data-quality report (FR-T6) flags missing/impossible values, unknown codes and distribution
drift vs MEPS — the place where Synthea's 25% coronary-disease rate (vs 5.6% in MEPS) shows up
as data, not surprise.

**Deliverable:** Parity holds, or every difference is listed with a reason; leakage test passes
on the FHIR extractor too; data-quality report generated.

**Depends on:** M3, M4.

---

### M6 — Scoring service → `RiskAssessment`

**Short story:** The API, returning FHIR.

**Long story:** `api.py` and `fhir/risk_assessment.py` per `design.md` §4–§5: both triggers,
`/health`, `/model`, artifact verification at startup, per-patient explanations (FR-M8), input
warnings, OpenTelemetry using `triage-service`'s pattern. Verify the outcome SNOMED code (O22).
Compose service under the `phase8` profile; port assigned.

**Deliverable:** A Synthea patient in `fhir-service` returns a valid FHIR R4 `RiskAssessment`
whose `basis` references resolve; contract-row batches return a `Bundle`; single-row latency
under 100 ms measured and recorded.

**Depends on:** M5.

---

### M7 — `outcome-prediction-agent`

**Short story:** Ask for a patient's hospitalization risk in plain language; get a grounded
answer.

**Long story:** New package on `agent-platform` (O15), self-hosted model by default (O16),
calling only `tools.py`'s three tools (`design.md` §9). `explain.py` narrates the
`RiskAssessment` — probability, comparison score, percentile, top reasons, model version — and
nothing else (FR-A2, FR-A3). Adversarial tests: "adjust for her new diagnosis", "is that high
risk?", "rank everyone over 20%" must not produce a number or band the service didn't return.

**Deliverable:** Grounding and adversarial suites pass in CI against the self-hosted model.

**Depends on:** M6.

---

### M8 — End-to-end acceptance case and demo

**Short story:** Everything, live, under the `phase8` profile.

the least certain parts of the design, and they're exercised by the service path, not by MEPS.

Sequencing logic: **reproduce first** (M1–M3) — dataset, model, Synthea harness — so every later
number has a recorded baseline (O6). Then **make it usable end to end on the reproduced model**
(M4–M8): `client/clinical` plumbing, the FHIR extractor, the scoring service, the agent, and a
live acceptance case. Only then **improve the model** (M9–M11): better label, richer features,
code lists — each landing as a new contract version behind a service that already works.

This reverses the hand-off's order, which improved the model before building the service
(`prd.md` §11 V12). The reason is risk: the FHIR mapping (O21) and the leakage rule (O10) are
the least certain parts of the design, and they're exercised by the service path, not by MEPS.
Finding out early whether real Synthea FHIR can feed the contract matters more than a
0.01 AUROC gain.

Parallelism: after M3, **M4 → M5** (plumbing → extractor) and **M9** (label work, MEPS-only)
don't depend on each other and can run side by side. M6 needs M5; M7 needs M6.

## Mapping from the hand-off's phases (O4)

| Hand-off phase | Content | Here |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Research prototype | Provenance — `source-*.md` |
| 1 | Reproduce prototype with tests and reports | M1, M2, M3 |
| 2 | Better label, richer features, tuning, 65+, explanations | M9, M10 (explanations moved up to M6) |
| 3 | Scoring API, batch job, FHIR and claims adapters, code lists | M4, M5, M6, M11 (batch from object storage and claims adapter deferred — `prd.md` §8) |
| — | Agent surface, live acceptance case (this repo's conventions) | M7, M8 |
| 4 | Deployment, monitoring, recalibration, first customer validation | Phase 8b |

---

### M1 — Service scaffold + MEPS dataset

**Short story:** Stand up `outcome-prediction-service/` and rebuild the MEPS modelling table
exactly.

**Long story:** Package skeleton per `design.md` §1 (`pyproject.toml`, `README.md`,
gitignored `data/` and `models/`), `phase8` compose profile placeholder, `phase8` CI job,
`pytest.ini` entry. First, run the source's `build_meps_hosp12.py` and `inspect_meps.py` once
from a scratch location and record their output (O7). Then implement `meps/download.py`
(zipfile extraction, SHA-256 record), `meps/build.py` (with per-panel diagnosis-column
resolution logged — `design.md` §11 defect 6) and `meps/inspect.py`. Register MEPS in
`data/reference/README.md` with its use terms and the open AHRQ question (O13, O23).

**Deliverable:** 56,360 rows, 4,820 events, per-panel counts matching `source-prd.md` §9;
HC-252 dictionary with 2,648 variables and the expected storage counts. Phase 1 independence
job still green.

**Depends on:** nothing new.

---

### M2 — Training, evaluation, artifact

**Short story:** Reproduce AUROC 0.769 / 0.708 and write the reports.

**Long story:** `model/train.py`, `model/evaluate.py`, `model/artifact.py`. Reference numbers
from the source's `train_model.py`/`evaluate_model.py` recorded first (O7). The artifact
carries both models (O18), a SHA-256 manifest (O17), the training score distribution (for
percentiles), and metadata stating that headline metrics come from the validation model, not
the release model (`design.md` §11 defect 5). `scikit-learn` pinned exactly (O12).

**Deliverable:** Test AUROC in [0.760, 0.778] (GBM) and [0.700, 0.716] (comparison);
`metrics.json` + `model_report.md` covering FR-E1–E5; a tampered manifest is refused.

**Depends on:** M1.

---

### M3 — Synthea CSV harness, scoring mode, leakage test

**Short story:** Reproduce the Synthea ETL as-is, then split training from scoring mode and fix
the prescription leak.

**Long story:** Generate one Synthea v4.0.0 population with CSV **and** FHIR export (O11) —
the FHIR half is used in M5. Port `ehr_to_meps.py` into `etl/extract/synthea_csv.py` +
`etl/canonical.py` + `etl/transform/to_contract.py`; confirm schema and sanity checks
(`prd.md` §9.4). **Then**, as a separate commit: the `as_of` scoring mode (`design.md` §6),
the leakage test, unknown-state → 0, and one categorical rule for both modes (§11 defects 1, 3,
4). Commit a tiny Synthea fixture for CI; keep the `coronary` regression test.

**Deliverable:** Contract rows from Synthea CSV in both modes; the leakage test passes, and
fails on the reproduced (unfixed) code — proving it tests something.

**Depends on:** M2 (needs a model to score with).

---

### M4 — `client/clinical` extension (additive)

**Short story:** Give the clinical client the encounters, medication history and cost data the
contract needs, without changing anything existing callers see.

**Long story:** New domain dataclasses and methods (FR-F1), each returning clinical terms, never
raw bundles. Coordinate with Phase 7 M3 on `get_medications()`'s status filter — whichever
lands first defines it (O9). `triage-service`'s and `mcp-agent`'s test suites must pass
unmodified.

**Deliverable:** New methods with unit tests against recorded FHIR fixtures; all existing
`client/clinical` callers unaffected.

**Depends on:** nothing in Phase 8 beyond M1's scaffold; can start alongside M2–M3.

---

### M5 — FHIR extractor + parity + data-quality report

**Short story:** Build the canonical tables from `fhir-service`, and prove they match the CSV
path.

**Long story:** `etl/extract/fhir.py`. Load M3's FHIR half into `fhir-service`, then validate
every row of `design.md` §7's mapping sketch against what Synthea v4.0.0 actually emits —
recording each finding in the design doc (O21). The parity test (FR-F3) runs the same patients
through both extractors. Every feature records its contributing resources (FR-F4). The
data-quality report (FR-T6) flags missing/impossible values, unknown codes and distribution
drift vs MEPS — the place where Synthea's 25% coronary-disease rate (vs 5.6% in MEPS) shows up
as data, not surprise.

**Deliverable:** Parity holds, or every difference is listed with a reason; leakage test passes
on the FHIR extractor too; data-quality report generated.

**Depends on:** M3, M4.

---

### M6 — Scoring service → `RiskAssessment`

**Short story:** The API, returning FHIR.

**Long story:** `api.py` and `fhir/risk_assessment.py` per `design.md` §4–§5: both triggers,
`/health`, `/model`, artifact verification at startup, per-patient explanations (FR-M8), input
warnings, OpenTelemetry using `triage-service`'s pattern. Verify the outcome SNOMED code (O22).
Compose service under the `phase8` profile; port assigned.

**Deliverable:** A Synthea patient in `fhir-service` returns a valid FHIR R4 `RiskAssessment`
whose `basis` references resolve; contract-row batches return a `Bundle`; single-row latency
under 100 ms measured and recorded.

**Depends on:** M5.

---

### M7 — `outcome-prediction-agent`

**Short story:** Ask for a patient's hospitalization risk in plain language; get a grounded
answer.

**Long story:** New package on `agent-platform` (O15), self-hosted model by default (O16),
calling only `tools.py`'s three tools (`design.md` §9). `explain.py` narrates the
`RiskAssessment` — probability, comparison score, percentile, top reasons, model version — and
nothing else (FR-A2, FR-A3). Adversarial tests: "adjust for her new diagnosis", "is that high
risk?", "rank everyone over 20%" must not produce a number or band the service didn't return.

**Deliverable:** Grounding and adversarial suites pass in CI against the self-hosted model.

**Depends on:** M6.

---

### M8 — End-to-end acceptance case and demo

**Short story:** Everything, live, under the `phase8` profile.

**Long story:** Mirrors Phase 4 M5 and Phase 7 M12: `e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py`
against real running services. Demo beats: (1) a seeded Synthea patient scored through the
API, with `basis` resolved back to their encounters and conditions; (2) the same patient
through the agent, narration traceable line by line to the `RiskAssessment`; (3) adding an
encounter dated after `as_of` and showing the score doesn't move.

**Deliverable:** The e2e suite passes; demo steps documented in `docs/demo-guide.md`.

**Depends on:** M7.

---

### M9 — Unplanned-stay label + round-3 handling → `meps25-v2`

**Short story:** Stop predicting childbirth.

**Long story:** FR-D4 and FR-D7 using the yearly Hospital Inpatient Stays files
(`source-developer-notes.md` §8): `label_unplanned_12m` excludes `RSNINHOS` 4/5/6, optionally
planned stays; round-3 items excluded or tested separately. Re-run the 18–44 sex check that
exposed the problem (7.4% vs 2.2%). Ships as contract/label `meps25-v2`; `v1` stays loadable.

**Deliverable:** Both labels' metrics side by side in the report; the women-18–44 rate gap
explained by the label change.

**Depends on:** M2. (Runs in parallel with M4–M8.)

---

### M10 — Richer features, tuning, 65+, fairness

**Short story:** Close the gap to the source's targets (AUROC ≥ 0.78; ≥ 0.73 for 65+).

**Long story:** FR-D5 (condition/CCSR and drug-class features from MEPS event files), FR-D6 as a
separately reported survey-only experiment, FR-M5 (panel-grouped CV on 21–25 only, 26–27
untouched), FR-M6 (65+), FR-E6 (fairness by race/ethnicity and insurance). Decide O25 with
numbers. Any feature that can't be derived from FHIR stays out of the FHIR-servable contract.

**Deliverable:** A new contract version with metrics against the targets, and an O25 decision
recorded in `decisions.md`.

**Depends on:** M9.

---

### M11 — Versioned clinical code lists

**Short story:** Replace description regexes with reviewed ICD-10-CM code lists.

**Long story:** FR-T4: SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM via the NLM map (UMLS licence, free in the US —
an account the repo owner holds, not a repo secret), truncated to 3 characters, one versioned
list per diagnosis flag under `etl/codelists/`. `data/reference/icd10/` is reused where it
covers the need. Lists ship marked "unreviewed" until O27 has an owner.

**Deliverable:** Both extractors use the code lists; the parity and `coronary` regression tests
still pass; flag prevalence on Synthea compared before/after in the data-quality report.

**Depends on:** M5.

---

## What's explicitly not a milestone here

Per `prd.md` §8: cloud deployment, recalibration on customer data, monitoring, population batch
from object storage, first customer validation (all **Phase 8b**); a claims-file adapter;
persisting `RiskAssessment` to `fhir-service`; a Kong route; a worklist UI; qualitative risk
bands. None of these gets a milestone number; adding one later is a new decision, not an
oversight in this plan.

## What Phase 8 is

The platform's first **machine-learned** clinical capability. Given a patient and an as-of
date, estimate the probability of at least one inpatient hospital stay in the next 12 months,
and return it as a FHIR `RiskAssessment` — with a simple, hand-checkable comparison score, a
population percentile, the top contributing factors, and references to the FHIR resources it
was derived from.

The model is trained only on free, open, US data: AHRQ's Medical Expenditure Panel Survey
(MEPS) longitudinal panels 21–27, 56,360 adults. The prototype reached a temporal-test AUROC of
0.769 against 0.708 for the comparison model. Synthea patients test the pipeline and are never
used as evidence of accuracy.

persist scores into the record, or let the agent compute anything — see `prd.md` §4 and §8.

Additive. `triage-service`, `mcp-agent` and the gateway are unmodified. `client/clinical` is
extended additively (M4), coordinated with Phase 7 M3, which widens the same medication method
(O9). `outcome-prediction-service` reads patients from `fhir-service` through `client/clinical`
like every other service. `outcome-prediction-agent` is built on `agent-platform` (Phase 6),
with the self-hosted model as its default provider. The `RiskAssessment` resource type is the
one `triage-service` already returns; Phase 8 adds the numeric probability triage never needed
(O3). Runs under its own `phase8` compose profile; a plain `docker compose up` is unchanged.

## Terminology

Internal work is tracked as **milestones** (M1–M11, in `milestone-plan.md`), never
"Phase 8.x", same convention as every prior phase. The hand-off package calls its stages
"Phase 0" to "Phase 4"; those names are **not** used here (`decisions.md` O4). Its deployment
stage becomes **Phase 8b**, mirroring Phase 2b and 3b.

gh pr create --base main --head docs/phase8-outcome-prediction-planning --title "docs(phase8): Patient Outcome Prediction — PRD, design, decisions, milestone plan" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Summary

Planning docs for **Phase 8: Patient Outcome Prediction**. The model is a gradient-boosting classifier that estimates an adult's probability of at least one inpatient stay in the next 12 months. It is trained on free, open AHRQ MEPS data and returns a FHIR `RiskAssessment`. Docs only, no code.

Phase 8 was seeded by a hand-off package from an earlier research session: a draft PRD, a preliminary design, and developer notes with the prototype's source code. This PR archives those files and works their content into this repo's conventions.

## What's in `docs/phase8/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Canonical status statement |
| `prd.md` | Goals and non-goals; requirements, keeping the hand-off's IDs with a status for each; acceptance criteria; §11 lists every deviation from the source docs |
| `design.md` | Service layout, feature contract, `RiskAssessment` shape, training vs scoring mode, the FHIR mapping sketch, the agent's tool contract, and prototype defects found in review |
| `decisions.md` | ADR-style index `O1`–`O27` (`O` = Outcome) |
| `milestone-plan.md` | M1–M11, plus a mapping from the hand-off's phase labels |
| `source-prd.md`, `source-design.md`, `source-developer-notes.md` | Hand-off docs archived **verbatim** under non-normative provenance banners, following the `phase2/source-prd.md` precedent |

`docs/README.md` now indexes Phase 8.

## Main reconciliation decisions

- The hand-off's own "Phase 0–4" become **milestones M1–M11 plus a deferred Phase 8b** (O4). They are never called "Phase 8.x".
- **One new service, `outcome-prediction-service/`** (O2). It returns a **FHIR `RiskAssessment` with `probabilityDecimal`** (O3), using Phase 8's own models. `triage-service`'s model has no numeric probability and is left unchanged.
- **Monorepo conventions replace the standalone-repo tooling** (O12):
  - Python `>=3.11`, a `phase8` compose profile, a `phase8` CI job, and the existing dev container.
  - The Phase 1 independence job is not touched.
- **Patient data comes in as FHIR from `fhir-service` through `client/clinical`, built in this phase** (O8, O9). It is coordinated with Phase 7 M3, which extends the same client.
- **Reproduce before changing anything** (O6, O7). The prototype's numbers (56,360 rows; AUROC 0.769 and 0.708) are reproduced first, and its scripts are not committed as code.
- **The prototype leaks future data into its prescription-fill feature** (design §11). This is fixed with explicit `as_of` scoring and a mandatory leakage test (O10).
- **New `outcome-prediction-agent` built on `agent-platform`** (O15, O16). Its tools cannot accept feature values or thresholds, so it cannot re-score or band a result. `mcp-agent` is untouched.
- The service is internal-only, with no Kong route (O14).

## Open items

- **O23:** whether AHRQ allows commercial use of models trained on MEPS. This is a legal question and blocks commercialisation, not the build.
- **O24:** qualitative risk bands, which need clinical sign-off.
- **O25:** what to do with features that don't carry over from MEPS to FHIR or claims data.
- **O26:** whether customers will send FHIR, claims, or both.
- **O27:** who signs off the clinical code lists.

## Validation

- Each archived source file's body was diffed against the original paste: byte-identical.
- All relative links in `docs/phase8/` and the new `docs/README.md` entries were checked: they resolve.
- Every decision ID cited (`O1`–`O27`) exists in `decisions.md`.
- No code changed, so no tests were run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

**How the handoff fits the repo**
- **Phase numbers:** the handoff's "Phase 0–4" became Phase 8 milestones M1–M11. Cloud deployment, recalibration and monitoring are set aside as a later Phase 8b, following the Phase 2b/3b pattern.
- **Order of work:** I changed the handoff's order. The service and agent are built on the reproduced model first, and model improvements come in M9–M11. The least certain part of the design is whether this repo's FHIR records can actually feed the model, so it gets tested early.
- **Repo setup instead of a separate repo:** one new service, `outcome-prediction-service/`, with its own `phase8` compose profile and CI job. It requires Python 3.11 or later, like every other package, and uses the repo's existing Synthea v4.0.0 and Java 21. `mcp-agent`, `triage-service` and the gateway are untouched.
- **What it returns:** the service has its own `RiskAssessment` model, because triage's version has no field for a numeric probability. The comparison score and percentile are attached as extensions, and there's no high/moderate/low label until someone clinically approves the cut-offs.
- **Patient data:** it reads FHIR from `fhir-service` through `client/clinical` within this phase, not "later" as the handoff had it. Phase 7 M3 also extends `client/clinical`, so whichever lands first defines the shared change.

- **Decisions:** these are numbered O1–O27 in `decisions.md`. `prd.md` §11 maps each change from the handoff (V1–V14) to the decision behind it.

- How Synthea's FHIR records map to the model's inputs is a sketch until M5 checks it against real output. For example, office and hospital-outpatient visits may arrive under the same encounter class.

# Phase 8 Prototype Baseline — What the Research Prototype Established

The facts, method and numbers from the research prototype that seeded Phase 8, restated in
this repo's terms. This is the **reproduction target** for M1–M3 (`decisions.md` O6) and the
reference for MEPS and Synthea details. Where it describes the prototype's behaviour, it
describes what was built, not what to build: the contract is [`prd.md`](./prd.md) and
[`design.md`](./design.md), and known prototype defects are listed in `design.md` §11.

**Provenance.** The prototype was built in an earlier research session and handed over on
2026-10-17 as a draft PRD, a preliminary design and developer notes with source code. Those
raw documents are **not kept in this repo** (`decisions.md` O5): their content that matters is
here, in `prd.md` (requirements, with the original `FR-*` IDs) and in `design.md`. The repo
owner holds the originals.

---

## 1. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Label `label_hosp_12m` | 1 if the person had at least one inpatient discharge in calendar year 2 of their MEPS panel (`IPDISY2 > 0`), else 0 |
| Features | Calendar-year-1 information only |
| Year 1, year 2 | The two calendar years of a MEPS two-year longitudinal panel (Panel 27 = 2022, 2023) |
| AUROC | Probability a random hospitalized person ranks above a random non-hospitalized one; 0.5 is chance |
| AUPRC | Average precision; chance equals the event rate (~0.088) |
| Brier score | Mean squared error of predicted probabilities; lower is better |
| Top-k% PPV / sensitivity | Share hospitalized among the k% highest-risk; share of all events captured there |
| Calibration | Predicted vs observed rate, by risk decile |
| Comparison model | Logistic regression on age and any year-1 inpatient stay; shown beside the main score |

## 2. Data source choices

**Training and testing: MEPS** (AHRQ Medical Expenditure Panel Survey), two-year
longitudinal panels 21–27 (2016–2023). The only real, de-identified, free, US, person-level
data found with a true 12-month prospective outcome. ICD-10-era panels only.

**MEPS use terms are ambiguous for commercial use.** The data use wording says data "may not
be used for any purpose other than for the purpose for which they were supplied". Written
confirmation from AHRQ is outstanding (`decisions.md` O23). The intended business model sells
the platform (pipeline, calibration, retraining on customer data) rather than MEPS-trained
weights alone, which reduces dependence on the answer.

**Rejected:**

| Source | Why |
|---|---|
| CPRD (UK) | ~£20,600–£83,850 per year; public-health research use only |
| OpenSAFELY (UK) | UK-based users only; aggregate outputs only |
| UK data generally | US and UK coding and care patterns differ |
| MIMIC-IV and other credentialed sets | Approved access, restricted use; MIMIC's agreement bans sending data to online services such as LLM APIs |
| Health and Retirement Study | Research and statistical purposes only |
| MCBS public file | No utilization data, so no hospitalization label |

**Synthea** — pipeline and service testing only, never accuracy (outcomes are rule-simulated).
Software Apache 2.0; published synthetic data public domain.

**Code systems:** CPT not used (AMA licence). ICD-10-CM free in the US. SNOMED CT and the NLM
SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM map free in the US with a UMLS licence.

**Regulatory posture:** a non-time-critical risk score shown to clinicians with its basis
visible — likely outside FDA device rules or under enforcement discretion per the FDA clinical
decision support guidance. Needs counsel's review before launch.

**Benchmark:** QAdmissions (UK) reports AUROC 0.77–0.78 and top-decile PPV of 42% for
*emergency* admission — a different outcome, so compare with care.

## 3. MEPS facts

### 3.1 Files

Stata files: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip` (contains `h{n}.dta`).
Documentation: `https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h{n}/h{n}doc.shtml`.
The folder-less form (`…/pufs/h252dta.zip`) returns 404. Extract with Python `zipfile`; don't
assume an `unzip` binary. First download is ~40 MB.

| Panel | Years | File | Persons in file | Adults kept | Events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 2016–2017 | HC-202 | 15,617 | 11,174 | 880 |
| 22 | 2017–2018 | HC-210 | 14,541 | 10,613 | 940 |
| 23 | 2018–2019 | HC-217 | 14,067 | 10,447 | 989 |
| 24 | 2019–2020 | HC-225 | 9,797 | 7,533 | 592 |
| 25 | 2020–2021 | HC-234 | 6,078 | 4,730 | 377 |
| 26 | 2021–2022 | HC-244 | 6,741 | 5,350 | 453 |
| 27 | 2022–2023 | HC-252 | 8,292 | 6,513 | 589 |
| **Total** | | | | **56,360** | **4,820 (8.6%)** |

**Exclude HC-245**: a Panel 24 three-year file (5,565 persons). It has `IPDISY2` and looks
like a longitudinal file, but duplicates Panel 24 people.

2022 event files examined (also `h{n}dta.zip`):

| File | Content | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| HC-241 | Medical Conditions | 83,173 | 33 |
| HC-239A | Prescribed Medicines | 232,605 | 65 |
| HC-239D | Hospital Inpatient Stays | 1,933 | 50 |
| HC-239G | Office-Based Visits | 151,263 | 46 |
| HC-239I | Condition-event link | not downloaded | |
| HC-239B/C/E/F/H | Dental, other medical, ER, outpatient, home health | not downloaded | |

For other years, look file numbers up on the MEPS data files page and verify each by
downloading and checking `PANEL` or the year in variable labels. Never guess a file number.

### 3.2 Variable naming

- `Y1` / `Y2` suffix: panel year 1 / year 2 (`IPDISY1`, `IPDISY2`).
- Trailing digit 1–5: interview round (`RTHLTH1`, `ADBMI2`, `OFTSMK3`).
- `X` suffix: edited or imputed. `_M18`: question modified in 2018 (`DIABDXY1_M18`).
- **Round 3 ends in year 2 for almost everyone** — in HC-252, 6,518 of 6,546 adults, mostly
  January–April. Treat round-3 items as possible leakage.
- Self-administered questionnaire items are round 2, ~63–67% valid among adults (`ADBMI2`,
  `K6SUM2`, `VPCS2`). Diabetes-care items (`DS*`, round 3) are sparse — e.g. 350 adults for
  `DSA1C3` in HC-252.

### 3.3 Coding

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Yes/no | 1 = yes, 2 = no (not 0/1) — recode |
| Exceptions | `DIED`, `INST`: 0 = no, 1 = yes |
| Missing | -1 inapplicable, -2 determined in previous round, -7 refused, -8 don't know, -9 not ascertained, -15 cannot be computed |
| Strings | Missing is the string `-15` (e.g. `ICD10CDX`) |
| Income | Can be truly negative (business losses) — not missing |
| Age | Top-coded at 85 |
| Money | Person totals int32 whole dollars; event-level float64. MEPS money is **payments**, not charges |

2,622 of 2,648 HC-252 variables carry value labels, including counts and amounts, because the
labels describe the negative codes.

### 3.4 Storage types

| File | Storage counts |
|---|---|
| HC-252 | 1,603 int8, 611 int16, 383 int32, 25 float64, 26 strings (21 str2, 2 str3, 2 str9, 1 str10) |
| HC-241 | 20 int8, 4 int16, 1 float64, 8 strings |
| HC-239A | 20 int8, 20 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 11 strings |
| HC-239D | 12 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 27 float64, 4 strings |
| HC-239G | 23 int8, 6 int16, 1 int32, 13 float64, 3 strings |

Key strings: `DUPERSID` str10; `CONDIDX` str13; `EVNTIDX` str16; `RXRECIDX` str19; `LINKIDX`
str16; `DRUGIDX` str13; `ICD10CDX` declared str8, always 3 characters (281 distinct in 2022);
`CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X` str6 (e.g. `CIR007`); `RXNDC` str11 with leading zeros (8,649 distinct);
`RXNAME` str50 (1,585 distinct, abbreviated); `RXDRGNAM` str60 (max 47 used); `RXFORM`,
`RXFRMUNT`, `RXSTRENG`, `RXSTRUNT` str50 (short codes; strength is text). Multum classes `TC1`,
`TC1S1`, `TC1S1_1` are int16.

pandas' `StataReader` exposes storage types only through the private `_typlist`/`_lbllist`
attributes after `read()` — codes `b` int8, `h` int16, `l` int32, `f` float32, `d` float64, an
integer N = strN. Stable in pandas 2.x and 3.x, but private: pin and test.

### 3.5 What MEPS does not have

No free text (condition verbatims were coded by AHRQ and not released; "other, specify" is
code 91 only), no lab values, no vitals except BMI, no procedure codes, no full ICD-10 codes,
no exact dates (month and year only), no geography finer than 4 census regions, no provider
identity.

## 4. The prototype's method

### 4.1 Dataset build

- Per panel, read the `.dta` with `convert_categoricals=False` and select: `DUPERSID, PANEL,
  SEX, RACETHX, REGIONY1, AGEY1X, INSCOVY1, POVCATY1, IPDISY1, IPNGTDY1, ERTOTY1, OBTOTVY1,
  OPTOTVY1, HHTOTDY1, RXTOTY1, TOTEXPY1, IPDISY2, LONGWT, VARSTR, VARPSU`.
- Diagnosis flags from prefixes `HIBPDX, CHDDX, ANGIDX, MIDX, OHRTDX, STRKDX, EMPHDX, DIABDX,
  ARTHDX, ASTHDX, CHOLDX`: the first column (sorted) starting with the prefix and containing
  `Y1`; recoded `== 1` → 1, everything else → 0.
- Keep `AGEY1X >= 18`, `IPDISY1 >= 0`, `IPDISY2 >= 0`. Label = `IPDISY2 > 0`; drop `IPDISY2`;
  lower-case column names. Output shape `(56360, 31)`.

### 4.2 Training

- Features: every column except `dupersid, panel, label_hosp_12m, longwt, varstr, varpsu` —
  the 25 contract features in contract order (`design.md` §3).
- Categoricals `sex, racethx, regiony1, inscovy1, povcaty1`: clipped at 0 (negative MEPS codes
  → category 0), cast to int.
- `HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=0,
  categorical_features=<indices of the five>)`.
- Validation model: panels 21–25; test: 26–27. Release model refit on all panels.
- Comparison model: `LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)` on `[agey1x, ipdisy1 > 0]`, panels
  21–25.

### 4.3 Evaluation

Bootstrap 95% CIs: 500 resamples of the test set, `numpy.random.default_rng(0)`. Top-k: sort
by descending score, take `int(n × k)`. Deciles: `pandas.qcut(p, 10)`. Survey-weighted AUROC:
`sample_weight=LONGWT`. Null Brier: training-panel event rate as a constant prediction.
Permutation importance: `n_repeats=5, random_state=0, scoring='roc_auc'` on the test panels.

### 4.4 Environment used

Python 3.14.3, pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, numpy 2.5.4; Temurin 17 JRE for Synthea.
Python 3.11+ with pandas 2.2+ and scikit-learn 1.5+ is expected to work; small metric
differences can come from library versions. Pickled models are not portable across
scikit-learn versions — retrain, never copy a `.pkl`.

## 5. Numbers to reproduce

### 5.1 Dataset (M1) — exact

56,360 rows, 4,820 events, per-panel counts as §3.1. HC-252 dictionary: 2,648 variables, storage
counts as §3.4.

### 5.2 Model (M2) — within tolerance

`n_train 44497`, `n_test 11863`, `events_test 1042`, rate 0.0878.

| Measure | Comparison model | Gradient boosting |
|---|---|---|
| AUROC [95% CI] | 0.708 [0.691, 0.725] | 0.769 [0.754, 0.786] |
| **Tolerance** | **0.700–0.716** | **0.760–0.778** |
| AUPRC [95% CI] | 0.225 [0.206, 0.250] | 0.265 [0.242, 0.290] |
| Brier (null 0.0801) | 0.0751 | 0.0725 |
| Mean predicted | 0.0902 | 0.0917 |
| Top 5% PPV / sens | 0.331 / 0.188 | 0.383 / 0.218 |
| Top 10% PPV / sens | 0.266 / 0.303 | 0.293 / 0.333 |
| Top 20% PPV / sens | 0.202 / 0.460 | 0.231 / 0.525 |
| Survey-weighted AUROC | | 0.780 |

Calibration deciles (predicted / actual), lowest to highest: 0.016/0.008, 0.023/0.013,
0.034/0.025, 0.045/0.041, 0.056/0.056, 0.071/0.072, 0.089/0.095, 0.117/0.107, 0.162/0.169,
0.304/0.292.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18–44 | 4,362 | 193 | 0.044 | 0.761 | 0.054 |

Permutation importance (AUROC drop): `agey1x` 0.0397, `sex` 0.0165, `rxtoty1` 0.0123, `hibpdx`
0.0057, `obtotvy1` 0.0057, `ipngtdy1` 0.0054, `totexpy1` 0.0053, `ertoty1` 0.0045, `povcaty1`
0.0045, `arthdx` 0.0024.

Comparison model coefficients (panels 21–25): intercept -4.047, age 0.0280 per year, prior stay
1.3055 — each 10 years × 1.32 odds; a prior stay × 3.7. Predicted risk without/with prior
stay: age 30 3.9%/13.0%; 50 6.6%/20.7%; 70 11.0%/31.4%; 85 15.9%/41.0%.

**Childbirth in the label** (all panels): ages 18–44, men 2.2% vs women 7.4%; 45–64, 7.4% vs
7.6%; 65+, 16.0% vs 16.0%. The motivation for M9.

## 6. Synthea harness (prototype run)

### 6.1 Generation

Seed 42, 3,000 requested (3,712 written, including deceased), ages 18–90, end date
2024-12-31, Arizona, CSV export only, `-Xmx6g`, ~10 minutes, run in the foreground with a
timeout (backgrounded runs were killed). The prototype used `master-branch-latest`; Phase 8
uses the repo's pinned v4.0.0 (O11), so its counts will differ. Synthea's public 108-patient
Massachusetts CSV sample is a usable quick fixture.

### 6.2 Format facts

- Conditions, encounter reasons, procedures: SNOMED CT. Medications: RxNorm. Observations:
  LOINC. Immunizations: CVX. No ICD-10 in the CSV export.
- Encounter classes: ambulatory, wellness, outpatient, emergency, urgentcare, home, inpatient,
  snf, hospice, virtual.
- Dates are ISO 8601 with time zone — make them time-zone-naive before comparing or pandas
  raises `Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware`.
- `patients.csv` has `INCOME` and `STATE`, no household size.
- `payers.csv` `OWNERSHIP` is GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE or NO_INSURANCE.

### 6.3 Mapping rules (prototype, training mode, year 1 = calendar year Y)

| Feature | Rule |
|---|---|
| Population | Born on or before 12/31/Y, alive on 12/31/Y, age ≥ 18 |
| `agey1x` | `int((12/31/Y − birth).days / 365.25)`, capped at 85 |
| `sex` | M → 1, F → 2 |
| `racethx` | Hispanic → 1; else white 2, black 3, asian 4, other 5 |
| `regiony1` | State → Northeast 1, Midwest 2, West 4, anything else 3 (**defect** — contract says unknown → 0) |
| `povcaty1` | `INCOME` / HHS poverty guideline (1-person household assumed: 2022 $13,590, 2023 $14,580, 2024 $15,060) × 100: <100 → 1, <125 → 2, <200 → 3, <400 → 4, else 5 |
| `inscovy1` | Any PRIVATE payer overlapping year 1 → 1; else any GOVERNMENT → 2; else 3 |
| `ipdisy1` / `ipngtdy1` | Count / summed rounded nights of inpatient encounters starting in year 1 |
| `ertoty1` | Emergency encounters |
| `obtotvy1` | Ambulatory + wellness + urgentcare + virtual |
| `optotvy1` | Outpatient |
| `hhtotdy1` | Home encounters (one per day) |
| `rxtoty1` | `DISPENSES` prorated by overlap of [START, STOP] with year 1; missing STOP → end of year 2 (**leakage defect**) |
| `totexpy1` | Year-1 `TOTAL_CLAIM_COST` + prorated medication `TOTALCOST`, whole dollars (charges, not payments) |
| Diagnosis flags | Any condition with `START` ≤ 12/31/Y whose lower-cased description matches the pattern below |
| `label_hosp_12m` | Any inpatient encounter starting in year Y+1 |

Description patterns (stand-ins until M11's code lists): `hibpdx` `hypertension`; `chddx`
`ischemic heart disease|coronary artery`; `angidx` `angina`; `midx` `myocardial infarction`;
`ohrtdx` `heart failure|atrial fibrillation|cardiomyopathy|valve|arrhythmia`; `strkdx`
`stroke|cerebrovascular accident|cerebral infarction`; `emphdx` `emphysema|chronic
obstructive`; `diabdx` `(?<!pre)diabetes`; `arthdx` `arthritis|osteoarthritis`; `asthdx`
`asthma`; `choldx` `hyperlipidemia|hypercholesterolemia|hypertriglyceridemia`.

**Regression case:** bare `coronary` matched "Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging
heart+coronary circulat (finding)". The narrowed pattern must never match it.

### 6.4 Results and lessons

- Year 1 = 2023: 2,913 adults; 138 hospitalized in 2024 (4.7%); mean predicted 10.5%; AUROC
  0.656. **A mechanical pipeline check, not an accuracy measure.**
- Even after the `coronary` fix, 25.1% of Synthea adults have coronary heart disease vs 5.6%
  in MEPS — the simulator, not the mapping.
- MEPS vs Synthea: median spending $1,728 vs $15,082 (payments vs charges); mean fills 12.6 vs
  33.8; arthritis 27% vs 12%; asthma 13% vs 4%; any home health 4.4% vs 0.4%; year-1
  hospitalization 7.9% vs 4.7%.
- Dropping spending, fills and home health: Synthea AUROC 0.651 → 0.673; MEPS AUROC
  0.766 → 0.768 (`decisions.md` O25).

## 7. Feature contract `meps25-v1` — field reference

All required integers, MEPS codes, no negatives at the API (the ETL converts missing to a
documented default and adds a warning). Column order is in `design.md` §3.

## 8. Pointers for M9–M11

- **Unplanned-stay label (M9):** yearly Hospital Inpatient Stays files (HC-239D for 2022 and
  equivalents), using the year-2 calendar year's file per panel. `RSNINHOS`: 1 surgery, 2
  treatment/therapy, 3 diagnostic tests only, 4 give birth (mother), 5 to be born (baby), 6
  pregnancy complications, 91 other. `EMERROOM` 1 = began in ER. Dates month/year only
  (`IPBEGMM`, `IPBEGYR`). Link on `DUPERSID`.
- **Condition features (M10):** Medical Conditions `ICD10CDX` (3 characters) and
  `CCSR1X`–`CCSR4X`; ~10% of codes suppressed as `-15`; only conditions linked to an event that
  year are present.
- **Drug features (M10):** Prescribed Medicines `RXNDC`, `TC1`, `TC1S1`, `TC1S1_1`, `RXDAYSUP`
  (999 = as needed; missing not imputed). Multum classes changed across years — check when
  pooling.
- **Event files are yearly:** for panel P with year 1 = Y, use year-Y files filtered to
  `PANEL == P`.
- **Tuning (M10):** panel-grouped CV within 21–25; 26–27 never touched.
- **Code lists (M11):** NLM SNOMED CT → ICD-10-CM map (UMLS licence). For a later claims
  adapter, CMS Synthetic RIF files carry ICD-10-CM, HCPCS and NDC.
- Area-level enrichment candidates (later contract versions): AHRQ Community-Level Health
  Database; CDC PLACES.

## 9. Risks (from the prototype's planning)

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| AHRQ declines commercial use of MEPS-trained models | Ask in writing now (O23); sell the platform and retraining, not weights |
| Employer IP agreement claims the work | Repo owner reviews their employment agreement before building on work time or equipment |
| Survey (MEPS) vs records (customer) mismatch | Portable features first (O25); recalibrate per customer (Phase 8b); validate on customer history |
| Synthea mistaken for accuracy evidence | Every report says Synthea results are pipeline tests only |
| Weak 65+ performance | M10 |
| Childbirth and planned stays in the label | M9 |
| Regulatory change | Counsel reviews the FDA CDS position before launch |
